entry.title: Siemens & Festo | Industrielle KI revolutioniert die Fertigung

media:group.media:title: Siemens & Festo | Industrielle KI revolutioniert die Fertigung
media:group.media:description:
Wie wird Industrial AI die Fertigung in den kommenden Jahren verändern?
Bei Tech Minds in Erlangen diskutieren Roland Busch, Vorstandsvorsitzender der Siemens AG, und Thomas Böck, Vorsitzender des Vorstands von Festo, über die Zukunft von Künstlicher Intelligenz in der Industrie.
Im Mittelpunkt stehen Industrial AI, digitale Zwillinge, autonome Fertigungssysteme und die Frage, wie Unternehmen industrielle Daten nutzen können, um produktiver, flexibler und nachhaltiger zu werden. Darüber hinaus sprechen die beiden über Humanoide, Europas Rolle im globalen KI-Wettbewerb, digitale Souveränität und die Qualifikationen, die künftig in Industrie und Engineering gefragt sein werden.
Speaker Roland Busch, Vorstandsvorsitzender Siemens AG Thomas Böck, Vorsitzender des Vorstands von Festo

entry.title: Pergamon Altar Digital: Gods and Giants in Photorealistic 3D

media:group.media:title: Pergamon Altar Digital: Gods and Giants in Photorealistic 3D
media:group.media:description:
The gods and giants of the Gigantomachy — carved into the Pergamon Altar's Great Frieze — have been out of public view for years. Through Pergamon Altar Digital, a joint project by the Siemens Arts Program and Staatliche Museen zu Berlin (Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz, SPK), the frieze is being recreated in photorealistic digital detail.
No tickets. No opening hours. No borders. Once the web version launches, anyone, anywhere will be able to explore one of antiquity's most dramatic sculptures, long before the Pergamon Museum reopens its doors on June 4, 2027.
Stay tuned.

entry.title: Inside the Alps' Most Futuristic Mountain Hut

media:group.media:title: Inside the Alps' Most Futuristic Mountain Hut
media:group.media:description:
At 2,883 meters in the Swiss Alps, the Monte Rosa Hut has no power grid, no public water supply and no road, yet it comfortably shelters up to 120 guests and generates more than 90 percent of its own energy. This video follows a hiking crew on the multi-hour glacier trek to the hut to see how Siemens building technology keeps this remote smart building running, even when it is buried in snow and unreachable for weeks.
Explore Siemens Building X: https://www.siemens.com/en-us/products/building-x/
The journey starts with Dr. Thomas Exner, an internationally certified mountain guide and meteorologist, who explains what makes this high-altitude route so demanding and how quickly the surrounding glaciers are retreating. Once at the hut, Fabian Gerschwiler from Siemens shows how more than 84 square meters of photovoltaic panels and thermal solar collectors supply electricity and hot water, backed up by 14 lithium iron phosphate batteries with a combined capacity of 215 kilowatt hours.
Inside, Siemens Desigo CC serves as the local building management system, giving the on-site hut warden a real-time overview of solar output, battery levels, water and heating systems. Layered on top is Building X, Siemens' open, cloud-based building platform, which lets the team manage the hut remotely through two applications: Operations Manager for alerts and daily tasks, and Energy Manager, which uses weather forecasts and expected guest numbers to predict energy needs.
Kilian Emmenegger, hut warden at the Monte Rosa Hut, describes what this looks like in practice, including a storm that cut power to the valley below while the hut, monitored remotely, kept running without issue.
The video closes with Prof. Dr. Christian Baumgartner, lecturer at the Institute for Tourism and Leisure at the University of Applied Sciences of Grisons, explaining why the Alps are warming roughly twice as fast as the global average, how retreating glaciers affect water supplies for up to 190 million people downstream, and why the hut's forecast-driven, resource-conscious approach could serve as a blueprint for sustainable building beyond the mountains.
For facility managers, building owners, and anyone curious about smart, self-sufficient buildings, this is a real-world look at how remote monitoring and renewable energy can work together in one of the toughest environments on earth.

entry.title: A new layer of management is emerging and with it, a new leadership challenge.

media:group.media:title: A new layer of management is emerging and with it, a new leadership challenge.
media:group.media:description:
People manage people. People manage AI agents. And increasingly, both work side by side.
On the Human x AI podcast, Stanford economist Erik Brynjolfsson describes this shift as everyone becoming the CEO of their own small fleet of agents.
But managing AI is only part of the story.
The real challenge is not simply plugging AI into existing workflows. It's stepping back to rethink why work is done the way it is and exploring what becomes possible when human expertise and AI capabilities are designed to work together.
